target_customer: SEC and FINRA regulated firms such as RIAs, private funds, hedge funds, broker dealers and fintechs that pay for compliance software
problem: Financial firms run compliance on fragmented legacy tools for archiving, supervision and employee and marketing compliance, which is costly and slow.
product_category: AI-native compliance operating system for financial firms

founders.name: Dave Feldman
prior_employers: Hive AI (led the joint venture with Bain & Company)
education: Johns Hopkins University, BS chemical and biomolecular engineering and MS computer science

founders.name: Ed Schembor
prior_employers: Amazon (search navigation product, Amazon Fashion catalog, internal ML team that became AWS SageMaker)
education: Johns Hopkins University, BS computer science

technical_complexity.rationale: Archiving that meets SEC 17a-4 recordkeeping, supervision workflows and many data connectors need careful engineering, while AI features are on top of existing models.

defensibility.rationale: Books and records archives and exam readiness make a compliance platform sticky, and regulated recordkeeping requirements are a barrier. Incumbents also own large installed bases.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent archive vendors and RIA compliance suites remain separate competitors. No acquisition found; Kroll announced a partnership.

market_need_then: Regulated firms must archive communications and supervise employees under SEC and FINRA rules, and the company says it replaces a fragmented mix of tools. Customer count claims on its site are unverified.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission statement of AI to increase human agency in support of a culture of compliance

branding.brand_signature: GreenboardGo AI harness for securities compliance

brand_strength.rationale: A clean short name on an exact .com, with trade press coverage and a Kroll partnership. Name origin is unknown, and old trademark records for the word exist for other uses.

outcome_analysis: Greenboard raised a 4.5 million seed led by Base10 in May 2024, then a 15.5 million Series A led by Base10 in May 2026, about 20 million in total. It claims 500 to 750 regulated customers and a Kroll partnership, and the team grew to about 35 people. Compliance recordkeeping creates stickiness, but archive incumbents and AI rivals remain.
notes: Seed confirmed by Pulse 2.0 and the YC page citing an Axios headline of May 8, 2024 (Pulse says May 15, 2024). Series A confirmed by Fortune, FinTech Global and Business Wire coverage. Customer counts differ between sources (500 plus versus 750 plus), both company claims. Competitor sources found are 2026 vendor comparison pages, not dated near the batch, so the list is empty.
